title: Integral operation projection in completed ordinary coordinates
statement: Fix a finite-field datum $D$, coefficient datum $C$ with prime $\ell\ne p$, and finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $H$ be the higher operation datum [def-sf-operation-stages]. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type schemes over the specified algebraic closure, $f:X\to Y$ separated of finite type, and $c=(X\hookrightarrow Z\to Y)$ a compactification. Choose any representative-normalized ordinary derived tensor models $a_X,a_Z,a_Y$ over the completed coefficient sheaves [def-pur-compact-support-completed-projection-data]. For arbitrary integral bounded constructible $K$ on $X$ and $L$ on $Y$, the ambient arrow underlying the operation projection of [def-sf-constructible-projection-mates] for $H.integralExchange$ is isomorphic to the arrow $\operatorname{integralMap}(f,c,a_X,a_Z,a_Y,K,L)$ of [def-pur-compact-support-completed-projection-data]. This compares two presentations at the same integral coefficient ring; there is no reduction-level parameter.

proof.text: Apply integralProperOperationProjection_isIso to the proper factor of the compactified identity square. Expand the supplied projection into the proper counit component, proper image of the supplied open isomorphism, and the compact-support endpoint isomorphisms. Every factor is invertible, so the operation projection is invertible. The cast maps in projectionComponent are isomorphisms as well.

proof.text: Compare the source objects. The support construction value equality and the qcqs support realization identify the operation support object with the ordinary proper/open image. Choose flat-term K-flat representatives of that image and L. The two signed-total representative comparisons identify the supplied ordinary tensor model with the ordinary tensor in constructibleTensorCompletion; its invertible tau then identifies it with integralCompletedTensor. Normalize H.integralTensor and apply the source completion-unit isomorphism from integralDomains.

proof.text: The independent concrete integral_isIso proof in SfProEtaleProjectionFormula makes integralMap invertible. If e identifies the sources of invertible p and q, set the target comparison to p inverse followed by e followed by q. The square commutes by cancellation. Arrow.isoMk gives the required arrow isomorphism. This uses only the existential arrow-isomorphism statement, without prescribing its endpoint components.

lean.statement:
theorem integralProjection_operationPresentation
    {D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}} {C : D.CoefficientDatum}
    {E : Type u} [Field E] [Algebra (Padic C.l) E]
    [FiniteDimensional (Padic C.l) E]
    (H : SixFunctorHigherOperations D C E)
    {X Y : SixFunctorSpace D} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsSeparated f.hom.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType f.hom.left] [QuasiCompact f.hom.left]
    (c : Compactification f.hom.left)
    (aX : SfProEtaleProjection.TensorModel C.l E X.obj.left)
    (aZ : SfProEtaleProjection.TensorModel C.l E c.Z)
    (aY : SfProEtaleProjection.TensorModel C.l E Y.obj.left)
    (K : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory C.l E X.obj.left)
    (L : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory C.l E Y.obj.left) :
    Nonempty (Arrow.mk (compactSupportProjectionComponent H.integralExchange f c K L).hom ≅
      Arrow.mk (SfProEtaleProjection.integralMap C.l E D C.different f.hom.left c
        aX aZ aY K L).hom)
